name: Advancing Global Standards in Childhood Brain Tumors at PNOS

content.title: Advancing Global Standards in Childhood Brain Tumors at PNOS
content.summary: The 6th PNOS highlighted global standards for childhood brain tumor care

media.alt: Advancing Global Standards in Childhood Brain Tumors at PNOS

content.text: The 6th Hybrid Annual Pakistan Paediatric Neuro-Oncology Symposium (PNOS), held over three days, brought together experts, clinicians, and trainees to explore the theme "Global Standardization in the Management of Childhood Brain Tumors." Organized by the Department of Oncology in collaboration with the Department of Continuing Professional Education at the Aga Khan University, the event reflected a collective commitment to advancing care for children facing one of the most complex and life-threatening paediatric cancers.

The symposium was led by Dr. Naureen Mushtaq, Conference Chair, Associate Professor and Consultant Paediatric Neuro-oncologist, and Dr. Bilal Mazhar Qureshi, Chair of the Scientific Committee and Assistant Professor of Paediatric Radiation Oncology. Under their leadership, the program was designed to address regional challenges while aligning with global standards of care.

Childhood brain tumors present immense challenges, requiring multidisciplinary collaboration. While survival rates in high-income countries have improved significantly, low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) continue to face disparities due to limited early detection, specialized care, and standardized treatment protocols. The symposium served as a platform to bridge this gap by adapting global best practices to regional contexts, ensuring more equitable and effective care pathways.

The program spanned a wide range of critical areas. Sessions addressed advances in neurosurgery, the importance of education and training, and strategies for capacity building in LMICs. Dedicated discussions also focused on supportive and palliative care, managing resource limitations, and the role of research and clinical trials in improving outcomes. The final sessions explored future opportunities in paediatric neuro-oncology, highlighting the importance of collaboration and innovation in shaping the next chapter of care.

Attendees included consultants, postgraduate trainees, medical students, and allied health professionals spanning paediatric oncology, neurosurgery, radiology, pathology, palliative care, and nursing. The diverse participation highlighted the importance of a team-based approach in tackling this critical health challenge.

Reflecting on the impact of the gathering, Dr. Eric Bouffet (Emeritus Professor of Paediatrics, University of Toronto) remarked, "The 6th PNOS stands as a powerful model for LMICs, bringing us closer to global standardization in the management of childhood brain tumors through collaboration, equity, and unwavering dedication to children's lives."

By convening local and international experts, the symposium reinforced AKU's role in the global effort to advance paediatric neuro-oncology. More than just a meeting of minds, it was a reaffirmation of the shared vision: to ensure that every child, regardless of where they live, has access to the best possible care.
